_note: Per-toy operating manuals for the VibeMCP server (tool: ToyHelp) - the SINGLE data source of the server. The server reloads this file from disk on EVERY call - new toys/manuals can be added without restarting the server. Structure per toy: type, functions (effect + scale), notes. All information verified on real hardware. NOTE: Toy IDs are NOT stored here - they are device-specific firmware values delivered live by GetToys/ListToys.

general.intensity: Intensity scale is typically 0-20 (0 = off, 10 = half strength, 20 = full power); pump functions only 0-3. The exact scale per function is listed in the respective toy manual.
general.duration: durationSec=0 means 'runs until stopped' - use deliberately and tell the user! Finite durations are enforced by the toy ITSELF and it stops on its own - no stop command needed.
general.stopping: Stop a single function: send intensity 0 for exactly that function (other functions of the same toy keep running). Stop the whole toy: StopToy. Do NOT reflexively call StopToy after finite vibrations - it would interrupt the vibration still running.
general.parallel_operation: stopPrevious=False (default): new function runs IN PARALLEL with already-running functions of the same toy. stopPrevious=True: previously running functions are stopped first. Control multiple actuators independently = send one separate call per function.
general.motor_numbering: Actuator numbering (Vibrate1, Vibrate2, ...) is TOY-SPECIFIC - numbered actuators can drive different ends on similar toys. The 'functions' section of each toy's manual is the source of truth; never assume a mapping from another toy.
general.live_changes: The intensity of a running function can be changed live - a new command for the same function updates it without interruption.
general.strength_limit: The 'strengths' limit reported by GetToys (e.g. {"v": 100}) is the limitation configured in the Lovense app, in PERCENT - not a native maximum of the toy; it follows the app setting live. The command scale always stays 0-20. The limit is applied PROPORTIONALLY on the toy side - all levels are scaled down, not only those above the limit. The MCP server does not cap anything and passes the requested intensity through unchanged.
general.patterns: Patterns (SendPattern) always affect ALL motors of the toy - the Lovense Remote API has no per-motor targeting in pattern mode: the F: field of the pattern command only accepts function types, not motor indices; undocumented values fall back firmware-side to 'all functions'. This is a limitation of the Lovense Remote API itself, not of toy firmware - assume it applies to all toys. For per-motor effects: SendFunction with Vibrate1/Vibrate2.

notes: Sends WebSocket events (e.g. button-pressed) - ListenEvents(toy='vulse') works.
A button press on the toy ADDITIONALLY starts local vibration - with keepState=true the server immediately restores the previous state.
Sends NO WebSocket events - ListenEvents(toy='gush') never returns anything. Fully controllable via /command.
